speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) what is the current cost of training a teacher; (b) what is the average number of years that a qualified teacher stays in the teaching service; (c) what are the three main reasons for teachers leaving the profession; and (d) what is being done to motivate teachers to stay and make teaching their lifetime career.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) whether the annual resignation rate of teachers over the last five years compared to a decade ago from 2% to 3% is a cause for concern; (b) what is the resignation rate of new teachers within five years of teaching in 2015 compared to a decade ago; and (c) whether the non-teaching workload is a significant factor in teachers' resignations nowadays.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) in each year over the past 10 years, how many teachers have left the teaching force after their teaching bond ended, with a breakdown by teachers on the Postgraduate Diploma in Education, Diploma in Education, and BA/BSc (Education) tracks; and (b) of these, how many are (i) MOE scholars, (ii) having teaching as their first career and (iii) are mid-career switches to teaching.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Salaries are also paid to trainee teachers during their NIE training.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Typically, there would be an uptick in the resignation rate to about 5% for teachers when their bond ends.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The main reasons for resignations range from family considerations, such as childcare, to a desire for a change of job.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Workload is not commonly cited as a reason for teachers leaving the service.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) recognises that teaching as a profession is demanding and requires significant commitment and deep skills.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Many teachers have decided to make teaching their lifetime career and contribute to the development of our next generation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have consistently paid close attention to our teachers in ensuring that they are fairly remunerated, provided with developmental opportunities to grow in their careers and being taken care of in terms of their well-being.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: First, teacher remuneration is regularly reviewed to ensure it remains market-competitive.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Second, we provide our teachers with many career and professional opportunities.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They can develop their careers by taking up leadership positions in schools and MOE Headquarters, becoming teacher leaders or taking up senior specialist roles.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Ministry also provides strong support for the professional development of teachers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Academy of Singapore Teachers, professional academies and language centres, put together many programmes and courses that help our teachers develop professionally.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We also have various financial and leave provisions to support teachers who wish to deepen their professional mastery.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Third, the well-being of our teachers is important to us.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MOE is mindful of the high expectations of teachers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To address this, we have put in place measures to support and guide schools in work allocation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Schools also regularly review work areas that can be stopped if they are no longer relevant or meaningful, simplified to reduce duplication and optimise efforts, as well as share good practices to improve work management.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Are there any ways, after you have analysed data from those who are leaving at the end of five years, whether we can improve the selection process?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The potential teachers coming into NIE have a significant amount of orientation and counselling as to the demands of the job.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But the reality is that the person that they are at the point of enrolment is going to be significantly different after perhaps another seven to eight years of their life.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They may want to start a family; they may have different aspirations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The reality is that it has to be possible and acceptable for people to change careers as their aspirations change, as the needs of their family change, what they want to do with their life changes.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, to have zero resignations and zero people moving on to a different career would not be tenable or possible.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We want to have as good a matching as possible and the key point would be to ensure that people who choose a career in teaching have a good understanding of what it involves, and that we provide them the professional development necessary so that they can cope with the rigours of the job, which are demanding.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I may have missed it, but I believe that he has not answered the whole of my question.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Can I have the Minister of State to address my question, please?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Member had asked about the percentage who had left after the expiration of their bond.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There was a slight uptick of 5% immediately after the bond had expired.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think I had addressed that in my initial statement.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Was there another particular point that the Member wanted to ask?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I had asked for a breakdown based on the teachers on the PGDE and BA/BSc (Education) tracks, as well as how many MOE scholars have been teaching as their first career and how many are on mid-career switches to teaching.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I believe that the Minister of State has not addressed these issues.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: My apologies to the House for this delay.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I was in the teaching service for about five years.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Even though my ex-colleagues and I would frequently complain about workload, about students, but that really was not the impetus for any one of us to leave the teaching service.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Most of my colleagues who complain a lot are still there teaching.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Some of the teachers are particularly concerned about the workload and it is not unreasonable to be concerned, given that there are demands on their time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are concerns with respect to the amount of administrative overheads and MOE is trying to put in place some information technology solutions that should be able to address some of those needs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Those were some of the deeper analyses that we found.
